subject.title: [codex] Verify Telegram topic proof for cron delivery

question: Should OpenClaw adopt validateDeliveryResults as a public plugin SDK contract and intentionally treat missing or mismatched Telegram non-General topic proof as failure after the platform may already have sent the message?
rationale: The code can implement either design, but choosing a permanent SDK hook and changing upgrade-time cron outcome semantics are repository contract decisions rather than mechanical contributor fixes.

options.title: Accept the generic hook
options.body: Keep the documented plugin-owned validator, accept the post-send fail-closed semantics, and require exact-head architecture and regression gates before merge.

options.title: Keep validation Telegram-internal
options.body: Remove the public SDK addition and perform Telegram proof validation within its send path while preserving sent-before-error progress for core recovery.

options.title: Pause the behavior change
options.body: Close or defer the PR if an already-delivered message must continue counting as successful regardless of missing provider topic proof.

recommendation.title: Accept the generic hook
recommendation.body: Keep the documented plugin-owned validator, accept the post-send fail-closed semantics, and require exact-head architecture and regression gates before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal is recent review and decision history for Telegram topic-routing contracts and their General-topic special case.
